text_blocks.snippet: Law enforcement and consumer protection agencies report several active impersonation, bank, and rental scams circulating across Central Illinois.

list.snippet: Pekin City Official Impersonation: Scammers are sending fake invoices and fraudulent notices on what looks like official city letterhead to collect money, targeting individuals who recently appeared before the zoning board of appeals .

Pretrial Services Scam: The Champaign County Sheriff's Office warns that callers pose as the Illinois Office of Statewide Pretrial Services, demanding payment over the phone for GPS monitoring devices or supervision to secure a loved one's release .

Bank & FTC Impersonation Calls: Agencies like the Woodford County Sheriff's Office and CEFCU report scammers claiming to be from banks or the Federal Trade Commission, telling victims their accounts are compromised and instructing them to withdraw cash or transfer funds into Bitcoin ATMs .
DMV Smishing Texts: The Illinois Secretary of State's office warns of fraudulent text messages claiming driving privileges or vehicle registrations will be suspended unless action is taken.

College Rental Fraud: The Better Business Bureau (BBB) of Central Illinois highlights rental listings that reuse stolen property photos online to collect fake deposits and first-month rent from students and residents.
